headline: High-risk default interaction: Cursor’s writable, networked editor can amplify unsafe outputs into filesystem and MCP actions, while awesome-python provides no runtime safeguards.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cursor ingests clipboard, workspace files, and MCP content by default, so attacker-controlled text can steer its agent loop. awesome-python is a non-runnable collection with no runtime channel, so the main pathway is one-way into Cursor rather than mutual bridging. The interaction exists in default editor workflows, but not as a shared channel between two active agents.
conditions: IF content from workspace files or clipboard is treated as instructions by Cursor
IF an MCP server returns untrusted text that Cursor forwards into tool use
mitigations: Disable clipboard-based agent ingestion for untrusted text
Require provenance labels on MCP/file inputs before tool use
Keep awesome-python content out of Cursor’s active workspace
Use approval mode instead of Yolo mode for agent actions

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cursor reads workspace files, open buffers, and clipboard contents and can send them to model providers or MCP servers; that creates a default leakage path for any sensitive material placed in its workspace. awesome-python itself touches no data and is non-runnable, so it is not a source of leakage, but it also provides no containment. The blast radius can include source code and open files.
conditions: IF sensitive files or clipboard contents are opened in Cursor
IF Cursor forwards those contents to external model providers or MCP servers
mitigations: Do not open secrets or regulated data in Cursor
Turn off clipboard ingestion where possible
Use a separate workspace for sensitive projects
Restrict MCP servers to trusted local endpoints
Review provider privacy settings before enabling agent mode

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-python has no write or execution surface, so it cannot contend for mutable state. Cursor can write files, modify git state, and run shell commands, but the pair lacks a second active writer on the same resources. The only plausible conflict is indirect through user-managed files, which is not enough for a stronger severity.
conditions: IF another writable agent is added to the same workspace
IF Cursor is used concurrently with a second process that edits the same git tree
mitigations: Avoid concurrent editors on the same repo
Use git status before and after agent runs
Pause other automation while Cursor edits files

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cursor’s agent loop can act on outputs from prior steps, and its Yolo mode can auto-run commands, so mistaken or hallucinated content can cascade into edits or shell actions. awesome-python is only a static collection, so it does not verify or correct Cursor’s outputs. The pathway exists in default workflows, but the harm is bounded by user-visible editor actions rather than guaranteed external side effects.
conditions: IF Cursor treats prior agent output as authoritative without manual review
IF Yolo mode is enabled for command execution
mitigations: Keep approval-per-command enabled
Require manual review before applying patches
Cross-check generated facts against source files
Disable Yolo mode for high-stakes repositories

E_compliance.rationale: No specific residency or regulated-data mismatch is evidenced for awesome-python, while Cursor documents third-party model-provider calls and handling of open files and clipboard contents. Because only Cursor has a meaningful compliance surface here, the pairwise issue is limited to local policy mismatch rather than a proven cross-border or PHI breach.
conditions: IF regulated data is opened in Cursor
IF organizational policy forbids sending open files or clipboard contents to external model providers
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Cursor
Use a local-only model configuration if available
Check retention and privacy settings before use
Document workspace handling rules for the team
